claim: *Brownfield progress.* Representation reach and enforcement reach are independent axes. A system may be strong on either dimension without being strong on the other; the next investment should address the highest-value gap rather than maximize both indiscriminately.
topology:
A two-by-two matrix with two independent axes. The columns are enforcement reach —
    how much of the obligation surface is constrained, sensed, validated, or gated at a boundary —
    running thin on the left to strong on the right. The rows are representation reach — how much of the
    important system can be reasoned about through trustworthy externalized structure — running rich on
    the top to thin on the bottom. The four cells name a real state rather than a maturity score. Rich
    representation with thin enforcement: the organization understands the system, but humans still catch
    the violations. Rich representation with strong enforcement: a rich governed surface, trustworthy
    models and enforcement at the right boundary. Thin representation with thin enforcement: reconstruction
    plus a human gap, little externalized structure and little enforcement, so humans carry both. Thin
    representation with strong enforcement: direct or local alignment, where tests, sandboxes, and
    permissions govern what they observe directly and no rich model is required. The two axes are
    orthogonal and drawn perpendicular: modeling reach and alignment reach vary independently, so thin
    representation with strong enforcement is a real, healthy quadrant, not a way-station toward richer
    modeling. The cells are uniform, with no gradient toward the top-right, because the next move is the
    highest-value gap rather than a march northeast at all costs. A green top edge marks the cells with
    representation reach; a blue right edge marks the cells with enforcement reach.
required_terms: strong obligations gated at a boundary
Understands — humans enforce Rich models; people catch violations.
Rich governed surface Trustworthy models; enforcement at the right boundary.
Reconstruction + human gap Little structure or enforcement; humans carry both.
Direct / local alignment Tests, sandboxes, permissions govern what they observe.
Next move: address the highest-value gap.
bw_encoding: Black text and strokes, white nodes; boundary weight indicates emphasis or enforcement. Original dashed semantics retained per figure; no color-only distinction.
redesign: Layout reflowed for a 15 cm monochrome print column; color categories replaced by labels and boundary weight.
alt: Two independent axes of brownfield progress: representation reach crossed with enforcement reach
